target_customer: Restaurant chains: table service tablets first, now drive-thru voice AI for quick service chains
problem: Restaurants lost time and revenue on slow ordering, bill splitting and labor intensive order taking. The founder started from a bad bill splitting experience at a restaurant.
business_model: Hardware and software sold to restaurants, first with tablets at no upfront charge and payments take, later software and AI subscriptions
product_category: Restaurant technology, tabletop tablets then drive-thru voice AI

founders.name: Rajat Suri
education: MIT PhD program, left to start the company
founders.background_notes: Got the idea at a restaurant in December 2007 while at MIT, and waited tables at a local restaurant to research the business.

competitors.name: TableTop Media (Ziosk)
competitors.what: Dallas company offering a similar 7 inch tabletop tablet called the Ziosk

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom hardware tablets for restaurant conditions plus ordering and payment software required hardware and software skills; later drive-thru voice AI is harder.

defensibility.rationale: Installed hardware in chain restaurants created some lock-in, but rivals such as Ziosk offered similar tablets and sales cycles were long.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Point of sale vendors and Ziosk competed for tabletop tablets. Presto later moved toward voice AI and went public by SPAC in 2022.

market_need_then: Restaurants wanted higher check sizes and faster turns. The founder's own bill splitting pain and early claims of 10 to 12 percent more revenue per restaurant in 2011 coverage point to demand.

branding.name_origin: Presto is an Italian word meaning fast, with a connotation of magic, per a trade report on the 2018 rename.

identity.voice_and_tone: Digital meets physical for big chain restaurants

rebrands.why: Wanted one name for the business and the product and reflected a broader restaurant vision, per the CEO

brand_strength.rationale: Known in restaurant technology trade press but sources show little consumer recognition or community, and the 2024 SEC matter damaged its reputation.

pivots.from: Tabletop ordering tablets for casual dining
pivots.to: Broader restaurant automation including payments and later voice AI for drive-thru
pivots.why: Expanded vision toward chain restaurant labor challenges, per the CEO on the rename

outcome_analysis: E la Carte, renamed Presto in 2018, raised venture rounds from Lightbank in 2011 and Intel Capital in 2013 and sold tabletop tablets to casual dining chains, then pivoted toward voice AI for drive-thru. It listed on Nasdaq through the Ventoux CCM SPAC in September 2022, but the share price fell below one dollar, Nasdaq suspended trading in August 2024, and in January 2025 the SEC settled charges that it misstated how much of Presto Voice relied on third party technology and human order takers. The YC status still reads Public but it now trades over the counter or is deregistered.
notes: Directory status is Public; the company was delisted from Nasdaq in 2024 and filed Form 15 effective December 2024, so exit.type spac reflects the 2022 listing. Company website presto.com is live and lists a 10 million dollar raise in September 2026. The 2014 round of 35 million dollars (lead unclear) and a 30 million dollar growth round in February 2019 appear in single sources and are unverified, so they are not listed as rounds. Seed in 2008 by Romulus Capital and YC and angel money in 2010 come from a wiki style page and are unverified. Founded 2008 per Wikipedia and the YC page, 2009 per another source. Competitor entry has one source; Ziosk launch details from 2010 not found.
